| `textures/vanilla_replacement` | partial | A pack retexturing something VANILLA ships the file at Bedrock's own path - `textures/items/totem.png` - where Java wants `textures/item/totem_of_undying.png`. Neither the folder nor the file name agrees and nothing in the pack says which item is meant, so the path is resolved through a generated table (SC-120 section 2.1) and served as a replacement in the `minecraft` namespace. Resolved two ways, both checks. Through the texture key's own language entry where there is one; otherwise by matching the file name against Java's own item paths and taking only an exact hit - Bedrock files all seven swords under one `sword` key and picks by aux value, so the second way is what reaches every common tool and weapon. `gold_axe` is dropped because Java spells it `golden_axe`, and a near-miss is not evidence. JAVA ITEMS ONLY, which is the honest limit. A block's icon is drawn from its model rather than from a sprite, so a pack retexturing a block cannot be served by replacing a picture; those paths are absent from the table and the block keeps its vanilla look. Entity textures are likewise untouched. Bedrock also accepts Targa and Java reads no such thing. A `.tga` replacement is reported as SCE-2043 rather than served as a file the client cannot decode. |
